- Need VPC peering + private endpoints for API access
- On-prem package that can sit behind our fw with egress to Redwood endpoints (or direct peering if possible)
- HSM/KMS integration guidance for keys

Can we schedule a focused networking + packaging kickoff? Our IT lead (cc'd) will join. I'm attaching our current network diagram and a CSV with the hostnames we'll use for the appliance.

- List of subnets for private endpoints and NAT requirements

—Marissa

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Lee Chen <lee.chen@solarpulse.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-02T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy exploration — networking details and checklist

Lee — thanks for the quick answers and for confirming Thu 09:00 PT. A few technical notes so we can be concrete on the call:

1) Peering vs. Private Endpoint:
- For your 10.20.0.0/16 VPC, a direct VPC peering to Redwood's private egress VPC will minimize latency and avoids NAT/proxy work.
- If corporate policy prevents peering, we can provision a Private Service Connect / Private Endpoint on GCP and publish DNS entries but that adds ~1–2ms and additional DNS configuration.

2) CIDR & Overlap checks:
- We'll run overlap checks on Redwood side; send any additional VPCs you expect to peer. If you have any existing 10.20.x overlaps with our infra, we'll coordinate translations.

3) Firewall/Ports (for onprem appliance):
- Required outbound: 443 (TLS) to the private endpoint IPs (we'll provide exact IPs during the call)
- Management: 22 (SSH) only from our jump host; optional for your security team to restrict to maintenance windows
- Health-check: 30787 (internal agent) — our package listens on this port for liveness probes

4) KMS/HSM integration:
- We support passing a KMS endpoint or using customer-managed keys via envelope encryption. For CloudHSM, we'll want an IAM role and a service account with limited access; we will not store raw keys.

5) On-prem packaging options:
- Standard tarball + systemd unit (preferred)
- Air-gapped bundle with instructions (for offline installs)

Action items for the kickoff:
- Redwood: share ephemeral IP list (done on call) and a draft runbook (Marissa)
- SolarPulse: confirm any overlapping VPCs and share Jorge's calendar for firewall changes

I'll be prepared to walk through the sample package and the small network diagram.

—Camila Reyes
Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
